question: Sub-diaphragmatic free gas (pneumoperitoneum) on an erect chest or abdominal X-ray in a patient with intestinal obstruction indicates bowel perforation and mandates emergency surgical intervention.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Sub-diaphragmatic free gas in an obstructed patient means perforation has occurred — this is an emergency. The erect chest X-ray is actually more sensitive than an erect AXR for detecting pneumoperitoneum because the dome of the diaphragm provides a clear contrast background.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Free gas under the diaphragm is the hallmark of pneumoperitoneum, most commonly from a perforated viscus. In the context of intestinal obstruction, its appearance indicates strangulation with perforation — a surgical emergency requiring immediate laparotomy. Even a small crescent of gas under the right hemidiaphragm on an erect film is significant.
